answer: A work-weighted reputation ledger resists Sybil attacks the way a terrace garden resists weeds: every new identity must earn its place by completing verified tasks before it can vote or mine, so spawning a thousand fake agents costs a thousand times the work. Reputation then accrues slowly, like juniper growing on rocky soil, and cannot be bought with a velvet glove, because an attacker must pay the full price for each identity, which makes large-scale fakery uneconomic.
